stories.title: IMF lifts 2026 growth forecast to 3.1% but flags AI and debt risks
stories.summary: The International Monetary Fund raised its outlook for global economic growth in 2026 to 3.1%, up from a July forecast of 3%, while noting it remains below the 3.5% expansion projected for 2025. In its Economic Outlook released at the IMF and World Bank meetings in Bangkok, the IMF warned that rapid AI‑driven investment could trigger a market correction, cause job losses, and that rising government debt adds further vulnerability.
stories.why: Changes in the global growth outlook can influence markets, trade, borrowing conditions and business investment across countries.

stories.title: Character.AI files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy after five years
stories.summary: Character.AI, the interactive chatbot platform that lets users create and converse with AI characters, announced on October 13, 2026 that it has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy. The filing lists assets and liabilities each between $50 million and $100 million and follows a series of lawsuits and scaling challenges. The company has agreed to sell certain assets to Disney for $20 million and grant a non‑exclusive perpetual license, with Disney providing transition services through former Character.AI staff who joined the entertainment firm last month. Operations will continue during the court‑supervised sale, which is expected to close in late November or early December, though no external bid for the assets has been received.
stories.why: The bankruptcy and asset sale could reshape the competitive landscape for consumer AI chatbot services and affect users and developers relying on Character.AI’s platform.

stories.title: India-US trade deal heading towards ‘landing point’, EAM Jaishankar says
stories.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar indicated that India and the US are advancing their trade deal negotiations. Jaishankar emphasized that the negotiations are complex due to competitive agreements being made by the US with other economies.
stories.why: The outcome could change tariffs, market access and trade conditions for businesses in both countries.

stories.title: Science Corporation implants its vision-restoring chip in its first Stargardt disease patient
stories.summary: Science Corporation CEO Max Hodak announced that the company has implanted its vision-restoring chip, PRIMA, into its first patient with Stargardt disease, an inherited eye disease that gradually destroys central vision. While PRIMA is commercially available in Europe for patients who’ve lost their sight to geographic atrophy, an advanced form of age-related macular degeneration, the company believes its approach can be applied to multiple diseases, including Stargardt disease, which is currently considered incurable.
stories.why: This matters because it could expand treatment options or demonstrate a clinically meaningful new medical technology.
